key_insight: Faynt shows that a single Transformer policy can scale to all 26 Super Smash Bros. Melee characters and outperform many specialist and multi-character baselines after targeted post-training.
engineering_relevance: The work demonstrates a practical recipe for building fast, transferable game-playing policies by combining large-scale replay pretraining, curriculum-based RL, distillation, and inference optimization.
method: Pretrain 10M and 75M Transformer policies on ~840,000 human replays.
Apply supervised post-training with rank- and outcome-based curricula, plus 75M-to-10M distillation.
Run RL focused on Fox mirror matches and optimize inference for recorded game states.
evidence_signal: In the 152-game benchmark, the supervised 10M model won 69.7% of games, and after RL it won 240 of 244 same-character games (98.4%) against fourteen baselines; it also achieved 68/68 wins against a private zero-delay model.
watch_item: Results may be affected by the action-delay mismatch versus many baselines, and the authors note they did not isolate that effect.
paper_title: Faynt: Scaling and Optimizing Policies for Competitive Melee
